One slender slightly flattened reproductive axis bears6 subopposite pairs of short stalks with12 rounded slightly compressed recurved cupules in two ranks. Cupules have a small broad lip/opening directed proximally toward their stalk attachment, not distal slits or open upright cups; rounded surrounding bodies remain volumetric. Isolated reproductive organ, not whole-plant habit: no foliage, trunk, roots, flowers, fruits, individual subtending bracts or exposed speculative seed arrangement. Caytonia reproductive-axis reconstruction only. Leaf genus Sagenopteris and pollen-organ Caytonanthus association is supported by cooccurrence/cuticle evidence but whole-plant organic connections/habit unresolved; no attached leaves or whole-plant claim. Primary official compressed fossils and historic drawings constrain two ranks and recurvature; thickness/pose/palette,12 cupules and nominal5cm axis are artistic. Cupule is not an angiosperm fruit. Visible lip does not assert exact anatomical seed count.
